BA.rationale: Boeing's fundamental health is severely compromised. The company is unprofitable on a net basis (Q1 2026 net income -$7M, EPS -$0.11), generates negative operating cash flow (-$179M), and carries a dangerously leveraged balance sheet with $47B in debt against only $6B in equity (debt-to-equity 7.8x). While revenue is growing +14% YoY and operating income turned positive at $448M, these green shoots are insufficient to offset the extreme financial fragility. Valuation is hope-based at 79x trailing earnings and 30x book, offering a 1.3% earnings yield in a 4.49% rate environment—no margin of safety. The near-term catalyst (Q2 earnings July 28) is more likely to highlight ongoing losses (consensus -$0.27 EPS) and execution risks than to re-rate the stock positively. Persistent regulatory scrutiny (new FAA directive for 737 MAX), legal exposure (LOT trial), production caps, and competitive share loss to Airbus compound the downside. The balance sheet risk is existential—any operational setback could necessitate dilutive capital raises.

The 777X program... delayed to 2027, incurring over $15 billion in charges.
